Theme

Body, health & movement

symptom noun

also symptoms, a sign of illness, have symptoms, what are the symptoms?

classical

Cels. 3.2: dēcēdentis ejus notae sunt, they are signs that it is abating
Traupman 66, 388: symptom

nota, notae f.

noun, first declension

a sign, a mark; of an illness, a symptom

A mark or sign of any kind, which Celsus uses of the signs by which a doctor sees how an illness is going; Traupman gives it first for symptom. The illness goes in the genitive: notae morbī.

Other words

  • signum, signī n. — a sign, an indication

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cels. 3.2: acceduntque ea signa, quae priōre volūmine exposita sunt

    Celsus uses signa and notae side by side; see sign.

  • indicium, indiciī n. — an indication, evidence (of something)

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Traupman 388: symptom

  • symptōma, symptōmatis n. — symptom (in medical Latin)

    noun, third declension · also used · late Latin · M-O s.v. symptom: Caelius Aurelianus, Cassius Felix; in medical Latin since

    Greek σύμπτωμα. Late Latin medical writers and modern medical Latin use it; Lewis & Short does not have it.

Examples

  • ea vērō, quae contrāria hīs sunt, dēcēdentis ejus notae sunt

    the opposite of these are signs that the illness is abatingCels. 3.2

See also sign, disease, fever, ill, pain.
